edges.description: The progressive arteriopathy is observed clinically as stenosis of the circle of Willis and the terminal internal carotid arteries.
Reduced perfusion through the stenosed terminal internal carotid arteries produces ischemic stroke.
Rupture of the fragile collateral vessels that form in response to the stenosis produces intracranial hemorrhage.
The cerebrovascular disorder has cognitive consequences independent of recurrent stroke.
Dysregulated endothelial angiogenesis and vascular remodeling driven by RNF213 variants contributes to progressive intracranial arterial stenosis and collateral formation.
YAP/TAZ-driven VEGFR2 overexpression feeds into broader dysregulation of endothelial angiogenesis and vascular remodeling.
Chronic NF-κB-driven IL-6 amplification and inflammatory signaling in vascular tissue drives endothelial dysfunction, vascular remodeling dysregulation, and progressive stenosis.
Loss of NO-sGC-cGMP signaling is proposed to produce abnormal vascular remodeling at the internal carotid artery bifurcations, the site of the steno-occlusive lesion.
Gain-of-function anoctamin-1 activity predisposes to the steno-occlusive arteriopathy, with additional posterior-circulation lesions.

nodes.description: Rare ANO1 variants increase the sensitivity of the calcium-activated chloride channel anoctamin-1 to intracellular calcium. This gain of function predisposes to moyamoya disease and is reported with involvement of the posterior circulation in addition to the classic features of moyamoya disease.

nodes.description: Biallelic loss of endothelial nitric oxide synthase (NOS3) or of the soluble guanylate cyclase alpha-1 subunit (GUCY1A1, formerly GUCY1A3) removes signaling through the NO-sGC-cGMP pathway that controls vascular smooth-muscle relaxation, vascular tone and vascular remodeling. This is the recessive route to moyamoya angiopathy in this entry. A review of the two genes treats RNF213 and GUCY1A3 as joint regulators of nitric oxide-mediated vascular protection, so this mechanism is not necessarily independent of the RNF213 nodes.
